overview: This module is really just two potentiometers mechanically coupled at right angles to a single stick, plus a tactile switch triggered by pressing the stick straight down — moving the stick along one axis turns one potentiometer, moving along the other axis turns the second, and both are read as ordinary analog voltages. Center position doesn't read as a clean 0V/mid-voltage on most modules due to minor mechanical variance, which is why almost every joystick project starts with a quick calibration step reading the resting X/Y values before interpreting movement.
simpleSummary: A stick you tilt in any direction, read by a microcontroller as two simple analog values.

specifications.axes: 2 (X and Y), each a separate potentiometer
specifications.outputType: Analog voltage per axis, plus a digital button press output
specifications.restingPosition: Approximately mid-range voltage on both axes, but rarely exact — calibrate per unit

pinMap.name: VRx
pinMap.function: Analog output for the X-axis potentiometer.
pinMap.gotcha: Resting (centered) voltage is rarely exactly mid-scale — read and store the resting value at startup rather than assuming a fixed center point.

pinMap.name: VRy
pinMap.function: Analog output for the Y-axis potentiometer.

pinMap.name: SW
pinMap.function: Digital output for the integrated push-button, triggered by pressing the stick down (active LOW on most modules).

useCases.title: Robot/RC vehicle manual control
useCases.scenario: Two-axis directional control for driving a robot or steering a vehicle.

useCases.title: Camera pan/tilt control
useCases.scenario: Manually aim a camera or turret using X/Y stick position mapped to two servos.

useCases.title: Game controller input
useCases.scenario: Analog movement control for a DIY game controller, with the push button as an extra action button.

oftenUpgradedTo: Hall-effect joysticks (contactless, no potentiometer wear over time)
